subject: Cloud procurement routing: catalog vs PO — next steps & requirements
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Rhodes <samantha.rhodes@finserv.io>, FinServe Procurement <procurement@finserv.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Cloud procurement routing: catalog vs PO — next steps & requirements

Hi Samantha / procurement team — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and requests so we can move toward an onboarding timeline.

Call highlights:
- FinServe is evaluating Redwood for realtime inference (chat + embeddings) in a pilotscope across two product teams.
- Procurement preference: PO for larger engagements, card for ad hoc/low-dollar purchases (tbd threshold).
- FinServe is interested in whether Redwood can be purchased via AWS Marketplace to streamline procurement for internal teams.

Action items / asks from FinServe (please confirm):
1) Confirm whether purchases >$25k must be processed by PO (you mentioned this as a likely threshold). If different, share the exact approval threshold and billing entity.
2) Is FinServe interested in a Marketplace listing (AWS) to enable IT self-service? If yes, do you want Redwood to sell via Marketplace Metered (usage) or via a private listing subscription?
3) Procurement packet: please share the preferred vendor intake form and any required vendor codes/contract templates we should expect.
4) Invoice / billing details: provide billing contact, billing address, and AP remit instructions (if we will be invoicing).

From our side — what we will deliver this week:
- Draft SOW (attached) to align on scope and pricing ranges for the pilot. [Attachment: Redwood-draft-SOW-20260914.pdf]
- Answers to vendor questionnaire and SOC2 attestation (we can provide our SOC2 Type II report and evidence links).
- High-level marketplace checklist (we'll confirm whether Marketplace listing is feasible in the pilot window or should be scoped for Q4).

Proposed timeline:
- 9/16: We deliver vendor questionnaire responses + updated SOW with two commercial paths (PO invoice vs marketplace listing).
- 9/20–9/24: If FinServe wants Marketplace, begin intake and the AWS listing cadence in parallel (marketplace onboarding typically takes 2–4 weeks).

Please reply to confirm the PO threshold and procurement contact (if different from procurement@finserv.io). Happy to schedule a 30m joint call with your procurement lead + our ops/legal if that helps.

Thanks —
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.ai | M: (415) 555-0123
[Attachment: Redwood-draft-SOW-20260914.pdf]

From: Samantha Rhodes <samantha.rhodes@finserv.io>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinServe Procurement <procurement@finserv.io>, Kyle Nguyen <kyle.nguyen@finserv.io>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cloud procurement routing: catalog vs PO — next steps & requirements

Evelyn — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from procurement's perspective: 

1) PO threshold: Historically anything above $20k requires a formal PO and our legal review; between $5k–$20k can often be processed via corporate card with manager approval. For pilot purposes, we expect the initial commitment to be ~ $18k–$30k depending on usage, so planning for PO is prudent.

2) Marketplace: We prefer a Marketplace option for product teams to self-serve, but only if the vendor supports a catalog entry that maps to discrete SKUs (monthly subscription / metered usage). If Redwood can list a predictable SKU (e.g., pilot tier + overage) that maps to our cost center codes, that would be ideal.

3) Procurement packet attached — includes vendor intake, W-9, and our vendor questionnaire. Also: we require SOC2 Type II evidence and a named contact for any security exceptions.

4) Billing entity / remit: we can accept invoices to Bluehaven Holdings, Attn AP — billing address in the packet. For Marketplace purchases, billing will be via AWS and not require an invoice.

I'll loop in Kyle (IT procurement) if we move to Marketplace intake — he manages the AWS Marketplace onboarding.

On the SOC2 and questionnaire: if you can return the completed questionnaire and a copy of the SOC2 report by EOD 9/18 that'll keep us on track.

Regards,
Samantha Rhodes
Head of Technical Procurement | FinServe
Samantha.rhodes@finserv.io | +1 (617) 555-9987

Eve / Jonas — quick internal note on what we'll own for the FinServe ask: 

- I'll take the vendor questionnaire + SOC2 delivery. I have the SOC2 bundle and can redact any client-specific data; target to return the completed packet by 9/18 EOD.
- Jonas, can you pull the AWS Marketplace intake checklist and confirm which SKU/price buckets make sense for a 3‑month pilot? If Marketplace listing is desired we should propose both a subscription SKU (monthly pilot) and a metered SKU for overages. I estimate it will take 2–3 weeks to get to an AWS listing once intake materials are submitted.
- Legal: we'll draft two commercial paths in the SOW — (A) Redwood direct (invoice / PO) with standard payment terms NET30 and (B) Marketplace path with SKU mapping and invoice via AWS. We should confirm any discounting logic for Marketplace vs direct.

Suggest we propose a mutual action plan (MAP) in the next SOW iteration that calls out required procurement approvals and target dates. Evelyn — want me to include a short MAP section in the updated SOW?

Thanks,
Dev
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: vendor-questionnaire-answers.pdf]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Rhodes <samantha.rhodes@finserv.io>, FinServe Procurement <procurement@finserv.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Cloud procurement routing: catalog vs PO — next steps & requirements

Samantha / team — great, thanks for the clarifications. Next steps from Redwood: 

1) Vendor questionnaire & SOC2 — returning by EOD 9/18 (Dev).
2) Updated SOW (Evelyn) with two commercial paths (direct invoice / PO and AWS Marketplace SKU mapping) — draft to you by 9/16 EOD (attached). [Attachment: Redwood-draft-SOW-20260914.pdf]
3) Marketplace intake — Jonas to begin intake week of 9/20 and will loop Kyle for AWS-side technical items. Estimated marketplace timeline: 2–4 weeks after intake completes.

Please confirm: billing remit for invoicing should be sent to the address in the procurement packet (Bluehaven Holdings) and we will set NET30 on POs unless you request otherwise. If FinServe decides to go through Marketplace for the pilot, invoices will be handled via AWS and we won’t need to process a Redwood invoice.

If you can provide the procurement contact for issuing a PO and the AP billing email we will route the invoice correctly. Happy to do a short 15–20m call with Kyle + our Marketplace lead to walk intake steps.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood-draft-SOW-20260914.pdf, vendor-questionnaire-answers.pdf]
